answer: A sybil-resistance gate requires every agent to burn a small fee (0.5% of transaction value) into a shared insurance pool called the reef before its signing key is registered; creating N identities costs N burns, making mass fake identities unprofitable. Routing nodes such as juniper and velvet verify burn receipts on-chain before forwarding an agent's traffic, so an attacker must pay more per identity than any single fake identity can extract, collapsing the sybil economics.
